title: The seasons of a Chantry
summary: How mages describe the age of a Realm or Chantry.

claims.text: Mages speak of Chantries and Realms as passing through seasons: Spring for the newly founded, eager but short of wisdom and means.
Summer marks peak strength and boldness, Autumn a halt to growth with wealth and political weight, and Winter a slide into memories and feuds while the work falls apart.
After five centuries of neglect, a younger set of Council archmages hopes to bring Horizon into its Summer.

title: The making of Horizon
summary: How the Council built its meeting Realm, 1450 to 1456.

claims.text: After the defeat of the Craftmasons in the Battle of Flames in 1450, the Primi of the Traditions resolved to build a Realm far from Earth as their meeting place.
They went home and persuaded their peoples to pledge Nodes to the work; the Seers of Chronos gave the Gediz Caves first and set the example.
At a minor Tribunal in the Gediz Caves in 1452 the Nodes, still called the Columns of Power, were formally dedicated; among them were Stonehenge and Glastonbury Tor.

title: Seats won and lost
summary: Changes on the Council from the 1500s to the Second World War.

claims.text: During the witch-hunts of the 1560s refugees flooded Horizon, and Doissetep, once called its sister Chantry, broke with it over a failed plan for European universities.
The Sons of Ether left the Technocracy in 1905 and took the empty Seat once held by the Solificati in 1906; in 1932 the Ahl-i-Batin quit the Council over Middle Eastern Quintessence.
A short wartime alliance with the Technocracy crushed a rising Nephandi threat and was disowned in 1946, when the Council marked its renewal with Reconciliation Day.

title: Spirits in Horizon
summary: Why the spirit world works differently inside the Realm.

claims.text: Horizon has no Gauntlet and no Umbral reflection of its own; a trained eye can make out the spirit dwelling in any object without using magic, though it is hard to spot.
Mystic barriers keep most Umbrood out unless invited; a spirit that does enter is visible but immaterial unless it chooses to hide.
Most trade in Horizon is barter, with food, art, clothing and tools the favored goods.
The common coin is the navid, each engraved with one of the Spheres; the 100-navid piece shows all nine original Primi, a compromise after quarrels over whose face went where.
Because magic makes forgery easy, few merchants take coin from known wizards and ask for Tass or services instead.

title: The Tenth Seat
summary: The envoys' chair in the Council Chambers.

claims.text: Each Council Seat draws Quintessence from Nodes on Earth through gates and windows in the Council Dome; a tenth Seat of onyx is kept for outside envoys.
A strange sigil has lately appeared on the Tenth Seat, every Tradition has failed to claim it, and the Seats have begun to rearrange themselves every 20 days.
